title: Unlikely Europeans: The hidden voters who could sway France’s presidential election – European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: Drawing on almost 6,000 AI-moderated interviews from May 2026, ECFR argues Europe could be a defining issue in France's 2027 presidential election, but because it cuts across political blocs rather than splitting France pro vs anti. Pro-European candidates must address French euro-declinism, stop treating LFI and RN voters as equivalent, and exploit a European-security wedge inside the RN electorate.

themes.theme: Fiscal crisis Europeanises the French election

insights.claim: France's fiscal crisis is turning domestic questions about debt, spending and taxation into questions about EU fiscal constraints, the European Central Bank and France's credibility within the eurozone ahead of the 2027 presidential election.
insights.speaker: Paweł Zerka
insights.so_what: The 2027 French election could reprice French sovereign risk and OAT-Bund spreads if the campaign becomes a referendum on eurozone constraints.
insights.quote: Questions about debt, spending and taxation are increasingly becoming questions about the EU’s fiscal constraints, the European Central Bank and France’s credibility within the eurozone.

insights.claim: ECFR's research, based on almost 6,000 AI-moderated interviews conducted in May 2026 across six countries, found the French are the most negative about Europe compared with the British, Dutch, Germans, Italians and Poles.
insights.speaker: Paweł Zerka
insights.so_what: Weak French public attachment to Europe is a structural headwind for EU integration initiatives that need French leadership.

insights.claim: When interviews were coded by how people talk about Europe's future, only 12% of French respondents were positive while 45% were negative, tied with Italy for the most negatives among six countries.
insights.speaker: Paweł Zerka
insights.so_what: France and Italy, two of the eurozone's largest debtors, are also the most Europe-pessimistic publics, a combination that heightens political risk around fiscal rules.
insights.quote: France ends up having the fewest “positives” (just 12%) and, alongside Italy, the most “negatives” (45%).

insights.claim: 76% of voters who chose Marine Le Pen in the 2022 second round talk about Europe negatively, while the rest of the French political spectrum is mostly uncertain rather than positive about Europe.
insights.speaker: Paweł Zerka
insights.so_what: Pro-European candidates lack an enthusiastic base, making a pro-EU campaign riskier than in 2017.

insights.claim: Across the French political spectrum Europe is described in declinist terms, and the 'Europe can-do' spirit Macron embodied early in his first term is now marginal, with PS voters citing war and security, LFI voters economic pressures and RN voters immigration as Europe's main challenge.
insights.speaker: Paweł Zerka
insights.so_what: Each French bloc reads Europe through a different anxiety, so EU policy messaging must be segmented.
insights.quote: Across the political spectrum, the French tend to talk about Europe in declinist terms—pointing to a general deterioration or a loss of normality.

insights.claim: A pro-European candidate in 2027 is not destined to fail, but must win over centrist voters who are negative or uncertain about Europe by arguing Europe is indispensable to France's challenges and capable of renovation.
insights.speaker: Paweł Zerka
insights.so_what: The outcome of the pro-EU vs sovereigntist contest remains open, so French political risk should not be treated as a foregone RN victory.

themes.theme: LFI voters are not RN voters on Europe

insights.claim: Macron and parts of the French centre frame the RN and LFI as 'two extremes', but LFI voters are far more European in self-identification: 53% think of themselves as European 'a lot' versus just 13% of RN supporters.
insights.speaker: Paweł Zerka
insights.so_what: Radical-left voters are an untapped pool for pro-European candidates, which could shift second-round arithmetic against Le Pen.
insights.quote: 53% of them say “a lot” compared to just 13% among RN supporters.

insights.claim: Jean-Luc Mélenchon's positions on Russia and Ukraine, his Beijing-aligned stance on Taiwan, his opposition to parts of Europe's rearmament agenda and antisemitism accusations give mainstream candidates substantial reasons to distance themselves from LFI.
insights.speaker: Paweł Zerka
insights.so_what: LFI as a party remains outside coalition logic on defence, even if its voters are courtable.
insights.locator: There are good reasons why LFI

insights.claim: Centre-left and centrist candidates such as Raphaël Glucksmann, Gabriel Attal and Édouard Philippe who hope to reach and win the second round against Le Pen have strong reasons to court parts of the radical-left electorate.
insights.speaker: Paweł Zerka
insights.so_what: Watch which mainstream candidate captures LFI-adjacent voters as an indicator of second-round viability.

insights.claim: RN supporters are split almost evenly between those who feel European 'a lot' or 'a little' and those who say 'not really' or 'not at all', so being negative about Europe does not necessarily make them anti-European.
insights.speaker: Paweł Zerka
insights.so_what: The RN base is less uniformly Eurosceptic than its rhetoric suggests, constraining how far an RN government could confront Brussels.
insights.locator: 3. Drive a wedge within the far-right

insights.claim: RN voters who feel at least a little European are more likely to see war and security as Europe's top challenge, are more supportive of Ukraine, more confident in European solidarity if France were attacked, and mostly support common European debt to fund defence.
insights.speaker: Paweł Zerka
insights.so_what: Support for joint EU defence borrowing reaches even into part of the far-right electorate, which bolsters the political durability of European defence spending.
insights.quote: Unlike their fellow RN voters, they are mostly supportive of the idea of taking on common European debt to fund defence spending.

insights.claim: Around one-eighth of the RN's electorate is uncertain rather than negative about Europe.
insights.speaker: Paweł Zerka
insights.so_what: A swing segment of roughly 12% of RN voters could be peeled off by security-focused pro-European messaging.
insights.quote: Taken together, around one-eighth of RN’s electorate is “uncertain” about Europe.

insights.claim: Marine Le Pen is attempting a balancing act, targeting sovereigntists with plans to slash France's net EU contributions while signalling to security-minded voters through recent criticism of Russia, a 'grand écart' the author predicts could be hard to sustain over a long campaign.
insights.speaker: Paweł Zerka
insights.so_what: Inconsistency between RN fiscal-sovereignty and security messaging is a potential campaign vulnerability that could shift polls.
insights.quote: But this grand écart could prove hard to sustain over the long campaign.

insights.claim: Europe may matter in the 2027 French election not because it splits France into pro- and anti-European camps as in 2017 but because it cuts across increasingly entrenched blocs, so the race may be decided by European-minded LFI voters, Europe-doubting centrists and security-minded RN voters.
insights.speaker: Paweł Zerka
insights.so_what: Standard left-right polling may mis-predict the 2027 outcome; cross-bloc attitudes to Europe and security are the swing variable.
insights.quote: The battle in 2027 may be decided by voters hiding in unexpected places

insights.claim: ECFR used almost 6,000 AI-moderated interviews to conduct qualitative political research at scale across six European countries.
insights.speaker: Paweł Zerka
insights.so_what: AI-moderated interviewing is being adopted by policy think tanks to scale qualitative opinion research, a growing use case for AI survey tools.
